name: common
description: Common drugs are those which are well known and widely used among the drug community. This doesn't necessarily mean they are safe, but it usually comes with a longer relative history of use in humans with which to establish a safety profile.

name: psychedelic
description: Psychedelics are drugs which alter the perception, causing a number of mental effects which manifest in many forms including altered states of consciousness, visual or tactile effects.

name: stimulant
description: Stimulants excite the nervous system and increase physiological function.

name: entactogen
description: Entactogens (also known as empathogens) are a class of psychoactive substances that produce distinctive emotional and social effects similar to those of MDMA.

name: depressant
description: Depressants are drugs which reduce arousal and stimulation in the user, characterised by a depressing of mental and physical functions.

name: opioid
description: Opioids are pain-killing depressants which may also cause euphoria.

name: habit-forming
description: These drugs pose a higher risk of causing habit forming behaviour, take particular care with the amount and frequency they are taken.

name: research-chemical
description: Research chemicals are drugs with relatively little history of human use, and thus particular care should be taken if choosing to ingest them.

name: tentative
description: Tentative means that there is not much reliable information about it. This is often because the drug is very new. Information listed under these drugs should not be entirely trusted.

name: dissociative
description: Dissociatives are mostly NMDA receptor antagonists, these substances are hallucinogenic but different than psychedelics. As per the name, these substances create a distance between the user and reality.

name: benzodiazepine
description: Benzodiazepines are generally hypnotic or anxiolytic depressant drugs.

name: cannabinoid
description: A cannabinoid is one of a class of diverse chemical compounds that act on cannabinoid receptors on cells that alter neurotransmitter functioning in the brain.

name: nootropic
description: Nootropics (also referred to as smart drugs, neuro enhancers, and cognitive enhancers) are substances that purportedly improve cognitive functions such as memory, motivation, attention, and concentration, in healthy individuals.

name: deliriant
description: Deliriants are considered to be true hallucinogens, because the visuals they produce are hard or impossible to tell apart from reality; they are also known for negative physical effects.

name: barbiturate
description: Barbiturates (also known as barbs and barbies) are a class of psychoactive substances that act as depressants of the central nervous system. They produce a variety of sedative-hypnotic effects including sedation, anxiety suppression, muscle relaxation, and seizure suppression when administered.

name: eugeroic
description: Eugeroics, also known as wakefulness-promoting agents and wakefulness-promoting drugs, are a class of psychoactive substances that promote wakefulness and alertness. The best-known member of this class is modafinil.

name: hallucinogen
description: Hallucinogens are a class of psychoactive substances that produce powerful alterations in perception, mood, and various cognitive processes. Hallucinogens can be classified into psychedelics, dissociatives and deliriants

name: oneirogen
description: Oneirogen describes a wide array of psychoactive plants and chemicals ranging from normal dream enhancers to intense dissociative or deliriant drugs.

name: antipsychotic
description: Antipsychotics (also known as neuroleptics or major tranquilizers) are a class of psychiatric medication primarily used to manage psychosis (including delusions, hallucinations, or disordered thought), particularly in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

name: antidepressant
description: Antidepressants are psychoactive medications prescribed to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, OCD, and neuropathic pain (encompassing SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MAOIs, and atypical agents).

name: hypnotic
description: Hypnotics, or soporifics, are a class of drugs which promote and induce sleep. They are the opposite of eugeroics which promote wakefulness. They are commonly distributed in the form of pharmaceutical drugs prescribed to treat insomnia.

name: mood-stabilizer
description: Mood stabilizers (such as Lithium, Lamotrigine, Valproate, and Carbamazepine) are prescribed to treat and prevent manic and depressive episodes in bipolar disorder.

name: anticonvulsant
description: Anticonvulsants (antiepileptics) stabilize neuronal excitability to prevent seizures, and many are also used for neuropathic pain, migraine prophylaxis, or bipolar mood stabilization.

name: anxiolytic
description: Anxiolytics are medications used to relieve acute or chronic anxiety disorders, encompassing benzodiazepines, H1 antihistamines, azapirones, beta-blockers, and gabapentinoids.

name: antihistamine
description: First-generation H1 antihistamines cross the blood-brain barrier to produce anxiolytic, hypnotic, and antiemetic effects, alongside anticholinergic effects at higher doses.

name: analgesic
description: Pure non-opioid analgesics (painkillers) used for acute and mild-to-moderate pain, such as Paracetamol, Nefopam, and Metamizole.

name: nsaid
description: Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs / AINS) reduce pain, fever, and inflammation. They require strict minimum intervals between doses, must NEVER be combined with another NSAID or Lithium, and carry gastric/renal risks.

name: triptan
description: Triptans are selective 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonists for aborting acute migraine and cluster headache attacks, subject to a strict minimum 2-hour interval between doses.

name: corticosteroid
description: Corticosteroids (SAIDs like Prednisolone) are steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs with powerful anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive properties, distinct from NSAIDs.

name: gabapentinoid
description: Gabapentinoids are voltage-gated calcium channel blockers (alpha-2-delta subunit) and structural GABA derivatives, widely prescribed for neuropathic pain, epilepsy, and generalized anxiety disorder.
